title: Korean Empire
capsule: The Korean Empire (Daehan Jeguk) was proclaimed on 12 October 1897 when King Gojong elevated himself to emperor, asserting full sovereignty in the wake of the Sino-Japanese War and the Shimonoseki Treaty (1895), which had nominally ended China's suzerain relationship with Korea. The Gwangmu Reform program introduced Western-style land surveys, a modern postal system, and military reorganization, but Japan's victory in the Russo-Japanese War (1904–05) installed Japanese advisors and stripped Korea of diplomatic autonomy via the Eulsa Treaty (1905). Japan formally annexed the empire on 22 August 1910 under the Japan–Korea Annexation Treaty, ending Korean sovereignty for 35 years.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The empire's territory as the whole Korean peninsula is well established; the primary boundary uncertainty involves the Gando (Jiandao) region along the Manchurian border, which was disputed with Qing China.
